answer: Sybil resistance here works through a bond-and-graph rule: a new agent must post collateral and be sponsored by two unrelated agents whose own standing is old, so identity is bought with real reputation rather than minted keys. Fresh clusters hit a nadir of standing within a few epochs and get throttled, while an honest reef of long-lived peers compounds trust at every vertex where they vouch. Faking N identities costs roughly N squared in locked stake, which makes cheap farms unprofitable.
